content.text: Speed up the dedupe pass on large exports (audit_test.go). Leave internal/patches_legacy.go alone — it is removed next sprint.
Starting with the benchmark so I know what shape the input is and what "large" means here.
Now the implementation the benchmark hits.

The inner loop rescans every kept event, so it's O(n²) on a 500k export even though only events within 30s can ever match. I'll walk the events in timestamp order and keep a sliding window keyed by actor/action/target/hash, evicting keys once they fall more than `window` behind the current event, then restore input order at the end. `sort` is already imported, and the key lowercases Hash to match `sameEvent`'s EqualFold. Only dedupe.go changes — internal/patches_legacy.go stays as-is.
Running the suite under the race detector first, since the window map is new state.

Done. Summary:

- Only `internal/dedupe/dedupe.go` changed. `Run` now sorts an index list by timestamp, sweeps a sliding window keyed by actor/action/target/lowercased hash (matching `sameEvent`'s EqualFold), evicts keys that drop out of the window, and re-sorts the kept indices so output stays in input order. The old O(n²) rescan of every kept event is gone; `sameEvent`/`absDur`/`SortByTS` are untouched.
- `go test -v -count=1 -bench BenchmarkDedupeLarge -benchmem ./...`: all 8 tests PASS; BenchmarkDedupeLarge = 91.2 ms/op, 48 MB/op, 501k allocs/op on the 500k fixture. The comment in audit_test.go records a ~2.14 s/op, 1.1 GB/op baseline for the same fixture, but that was measured on other hardware, so treat the gap as indicative rather than a controlled A/B.
- `go vet ./...`: no findings.
